clue.text: Merry-go-round in use, enveloped in cheerful music

indicators.note: the word use is wrapped up inside the music word, so this phrase signals a container

parts.note: a carol is a joyful song, especially at Christmas
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fairground ride is running, wrapped in jolly organ music.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundabout at a fair with rising and falling horses is a synonym pair with this ride.

clue.text: See me in bed-a heavenly body

indicators.note: the word me is placed inside the bed word, so in marks a container here

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at the speaker lying in bed, oddly described as celestial.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy wanderer with a glowing tail orbiting the sun is one kind of celestial object.

clue.text: Lemon gone off? Have another fruit

indicators.note: fruit gone off has spoiled, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lemon has rotted, so the speaker is offered a different piece of fruit instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns LEMON plus GONE (nine letters) into the name of a small sweet melon; 'Have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variety of melon, a fruit other than the lemon named in the clue.

clue.text: Odd way to wander around

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to range is to roam or wander over an area

explanation.surface: Roaming in circles is described as a peculiar way to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odd is peculiar or unusual: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Anti-imperialist shows small hesitation seizing country

parts.note: little means small
England is a country of the UK
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: An opponent of empire pauses briefly before grabbing a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, a Briton who opposed expanding the British Empire; now someone insular and opposed to foreign ties.

clue.text: Conservative stands up to emergencies

parts.note: rises means gets to one's feet

explanation.surface: A Tory politician rises to deal with a series of urgent problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; 'stands up' is a synonym, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical moments of danger or difficulty are synonyms for urgent situations.

clue.text: Dock brief goes to excellent student

parts.note: curt means short or brief
A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords with the digit as a letter I
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A court brief is handed to a top-rated pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' is a verb meaning cut short, not the courtroom box the legal surface suggests; 'goes to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock is to cut short or reduce, as with wages or a tail.

clue.text: Second place! Strong desire to have reckless celebration

parts.note: Pl is the abbreviation for place, as in a street name
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A runner-up feels like partying wildly anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of extravagant, unrestrained spending or indulgence is what the clue calls a reckless celebration.

clue.text: Some extra weight carried in car

definitions.text: Some extra weight carried in car

parts.words: Some extra weight carried in car
parts.note: literally the reserve wheel kept in a vehicle's boot, and colloquially a roll of fat round the waist

explanation.surface: A motoring remark about the load a vehicle carries.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the backup wheel in a vehicle and a paunch of flab are extra weight carried around.

clue.text: Remote possibility this streaks through sky

indicators.note: a possible version of the word Remote is a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Something that flashes across the heavens is only a remote chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a fragment of space rock that burns up as it streaks across the night sky.

clue.text: Run back sick, having had a Mexican cake

indicators.note: back says the run word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone runs home feeling ill after eating Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TROT to TORT; 'having had' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin flat unleavened round of maize or wheat is the Mexican flatbread called a cake here.

clue.text: Airport building that is linked to computer?

explanation.surface: A question about a building at an airport and its computer link.
explanation.definitionFit: The passenger building at an airport, and a keyboard-and-screen device connected to a central computer.

clue.text: Version of Bible Irish opposed

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version, the King James Bible
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irish translation of the Bible faces opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being against it or reluctant: a synonym.

clue.text: Steers with look to centre of target

parts.note: steers are young bulls, castrated male cattle
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Cattle are driven with a glance towards the middle of a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'to' are link words; 'Steers' is the cattle, not the verb of guiding.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner ring at the middle of a dartboard or archery target.

clue.text: Assignation, but not with a good looker?

definitions.text: Assignation, but not with a good looker?

parts.words: Assignation, but not with a good looker?
parts.note: a romantic meeting set up between strangers, where neither partner has seen the other, read jokingly as a date with someone who cannot see

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about being set up with someone unattractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A social meeting arranged between two people who have never met, so neither has laid eyes on the other.

clue.text: Wanting companionship, Nelly collapsed when pierced by love

indicators.note: the scrambled name has the love letter stuck through it, so pierced by marks a container
a collapsed word falls apart and its letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A lonely woman named Nelly falls apart when Cupid's arrow strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges NELLY to LNELY, and 'pierced by' puts O inside it; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling isolated and lacking friends means wanting company: a synonym.

clue.text: Man is worse than alien

indicators.note: worse suggests the letters of the two words are in a poorer, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A remark that a person is more objectionable than an extraterrestrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'Man' asks for a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a male first name, so a man may bear it.

clue.text: Pressed on board?

parts.note: suggests sailors forced into naval service, but means clothes smoothed on an ironing board

explanation.surface: A hint at men press-ganged onto a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry smoothed flat with a hot appliance on a padded stand is pressed in this sense.

clue.text: In big dictionary,'glove 'is left out

indicators.note: the glove word is placed inside the dictionary abbreviation, so In signals a container

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary, a very large dictionary
a mitt is a glove, as in a baseball or oven glove

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the word glove is missing from a major dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omitted has been excluded or skipped: a synonym.

clue.text: Notes on undemanding pleasure

parts.note: D and E are two musical notes of the scale
light means easy or not demanding, as in light reading

explanation.surface: Some easy-going musical notes bring enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: the notes come first, then the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Great enjoyment or joy is a synonym for pleasure.

clue.text: A case of possession

parts.note: sounds like demonic possession or a legal case about ownership, but means the grammatical case showing ownership

explanation.surface: A tale of someone being possessed by a spirit, or a property dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this is the noun case expressing ownership, as in the English 's form.

clue.text: Anything in New York may be wicked

indicators.note: the word for anything sits inside the New York letters, so in marks a container

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: A suggestion that anything goes in New York, a city of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Badly behaved or mischievous, a milder synonym for wicked.

clue.text: Force learner to talk nonsense

parts.note: to drive is to force or push
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone forces a novice to speak rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; the answer is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To drivel is to speak foolishly at length, a synonym for babbling rubbish.

clue.text: Gives too much praise, notice, to poor salute

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: a poor version of the word salute is a badly formed one, its letters muddled

explanation.surface: A notice criticises someone for overpraising in a feeble salute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges SALUTE into ULATES; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to flatter or admire excessively, heaping on praise.

clue.text: Porter shows the way out

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel porter points a guest towards the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' is the dark beer, not the doorman the surface suggests; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter and stout are both dark beers brewed with roasted malt, close relatives.

clue.text: Creation, say, no one could have foreseen

explanation.surface: The making of the world described as wholly unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creation was a deed of the deity; also an insurer's term for an unforeseeable natural disaster.

clue.text: An arrangement of crowning glory

parts.note: crowning glory is a phrase for a person's hair, so this is a styling of it

explanation.surface: A grand floral or musical arrangement for a coronation.
explanation.definitionFit: A style in which someone's locks are cut and set, the hair being the head's crowning glory.

clue.text: Some held estates should be for the first-born

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Inherited land ought to go to the oldest child.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'should be for the first-born' as the definition, but 'should be for' is a link: only 'the first-born' substitutes for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest child in a family is the one born before any siblings.

clue.text: Cavalier man

parts.note: reads as a careless fellow, but a Cavalier was a supporter of Charles I in the English Civil War

explanation.definitionFit: Cavaliers fought for the king against Parliament in the English Civil War, so a Cavalier was a supporter of the crown.
